rows.stem: Which of the following is true for all values of \(\theta\) \((0^\circ \le \theta \le 90^\circ)\) ?
rows.solution:
Dividing \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) by \(\cos^2\theta\) gives \(\tan^2\theta + 1 = \sec^2\theta\), that is \(\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1\).

None of the other three is an identity: at \(\theta = 45^\circ\), \(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 0\), \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \sec^2\theta = 0\) and \(\cot^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 0\).

Strictly, at \(\theta = 90^\circ\) neither \(\sec\theta\) nor \(\tan\theta\) is defined, so the identity holds for \(0^\circ \le \theta < 90^\circ\) rather than for every value in the printed range; it is still the only true statement offered. This is option (C) \(\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1\).

rows.stem: If \(k + 2, 4k - 6\) and \(3k - 2\) are three consecutive terms of an A.P., then the value of k is :
rows.solution:
For three consecutive terms of an A.P., twice the middle term equals the sum of the other two: \(2(4k - 6) = (k + 2) + (3k - 2)\).

So \(8k - 12 = 4k\), \(4k = 12\) and \(k = 3\). (The terms are 5, 6, 7.) This is option (A) \(3\).

rows.stem:
For the following distribution :

| Class | 0-5 | 5-10 | 10-15 | 15-20 | 20-25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 10 | 15 | 12 | 20 | 9 |

The sum of lower limits of median class and modal class is :
rows.solution:
The cumulative frequencies are 10, 25, 37, 57, 66, so \(N = 66\) and \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 33\). The first cumulative frequency above 33 is 37, so the median class is 10-15, with lower limit 10.

The highest frequency is 20, so the modal class is 15-20, with lower limit 15.

Sum of the lower limits \(= 10 + 15 = 25\), which is option (B) \(25\).

rows.stem: The length of tangent drawn to a circle of radius 9 cm from a point 41 cm from the centre is :
rows.solution:
The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent, so the radius, the tangent and the line to the centre form a right triangle with hypotenuse 41 cm.

Length of the tangent \(= \sqrt{41^2 - 9^2} = \sqrt{1681 - 81} = \sqrt{1600} = 40\) cm, which is option (A) \(40\) cm.

rows.stem: In the given figure, O is the centre of the circle and PQ is the chord. If the tangent PR at P makes an angle of \(50^\circ\) with PQ, then the measure of \(\angle POQ\) is :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - circle with centre O, the tangent line RP touching at P, the chord PQ and the radii OP and OQ, with the \(50^\circ\) angle marked between PR and PQ; the stem states every value. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
The radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent PR at P, so \(\angle OPR = 90^\circ\) and \(\angle OPQ = 90^\circ - 50^\circ = 40^\circ\).

\(OP = OQ\) (radii), so \(\angle OQP = \angle OPQ = 40^\circ\).

In triangle OPQ, \(\angle POQ = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = 100^\circ\), which is option (C) \(100^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: A bag contains 5 red balls and \(n\) green balls. If the probability of drawing a green ball is three times that of a red ball, then the value of \(n\) is :
rows.solution:
There are \(5 + n\) balls in all, so \(P(\text{red}) = \dfrac{5}{5 + n}\) and \(P(\text{green}) = \dfrac{n}{5 + n}\).

\(\dfrac{n}{5 + n} = 3 \times \dfrac{5}{5 + n}\) gives \(n = 15\), which is option (B) \(15\).

rows.stem: If \(\theta\) is an acute angle and \(\sin\theta = \cos\theta\), find the value of \(\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta - 2\).
rows.solution:
\(\sin\theta = \cos\theta\) gives \(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = 1\), so \(\tan\theta = 1\) and \(\cot\theta = 1\). (For an acute angle this is \(\theta = 45^\circ\).)

\(\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta - 2 = (1)^2 + (1)^2 - 2 = 0\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: The sum of first 15 terms of an A.P. is 750 and its first term is 15. Find its \(20^{\text{th}}\) term.

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: Rohan repays his total loan of ₹ 1,18,000 by paying every month starting with the first instalment of ₹ 1,000. If he increases the instalment by ₹ 100 every month, what amount will be paid by him in the \(30^{\text{th}}\) instalment ? What amount of loan has he paid after \(30^{\text{th}}\) instalment ?
rows.solution:
The instalments form the A.P. 1000, 1100, 1200, \(\ldots\) with \(a = 1000\) and \(d = 100\).

The 30th instalment is \(a_{30} = a + 29d = 1000 + 29 \times 100 = 3900\), that is ₹ 3,900.

The amount paid in the first 30 instalments is \(S_{30} = \dfrac{30}{2}[2 \times 1000 + 29 \times 100] = 15 \times 4900 = 73500\).

So after the 30th instalment he has paid ₹ 73,500 of the loan. (The total loan of ₹ 1,18,000 is not needed for either answer.)

rows.subtopic: Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: From a solid cylinder of height 20 cm and diameter 12 cm, a conical cavity of height 8 cm and radius 6 cm is hallowed out. Find the total surface area of the remaining solid.
rows.solution:
The paper prints "hallowed out"; it means hollowed out.

Height of the cylinder \(h = 20\) cm, and its radius is \(\dfrac{12}{2} = 6\) cm, which is also the radius r of the cone. The height of the cone is 8 cm.

Slant height of the cone \(l = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = 10\) cm.

The cone's base has the same radius as the cylinder, so the whole top face is removed. The remaining solid is bounded by the curved surface of the cylinder, its bottom base and the curved surface of the conical cavity.

Total surface area \(= 2\pi rh + \pi rl + \pi r^2 = \pi r(2h + l + r)\)

\(= \dfrac{22}{7} \times 6 \times (2 \times 20 + 10 + 6) = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 6 \times 56 = 22 \times 6 \times 8 = 1056\) cm\(^2\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(\angle ADC = \angle BCA\) ; prove that \(\Delta ACB \sim \Delta ADC\). Hence find BD if AC = 8 cm and AD = 3 cm.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - triangle ACB with D on the base AB between A and B, the segment CD drawn, and the equal angles ADC and BCA marked with arcs; that D lies on AB (so BD = AB - AD) is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
From the figure, D lies on AB between A and B, and CD is joined.

In triangles ACB and ADC:

\(\angle ACB = \angle ADC\) (given), and \(\angle A = \angle A\) (common).

So \(\Delta ACB \sim \Delta ADC\) (AA similarity), with A matching A, C matching D and B matching C.

Their corresponding sides are proportional: \(\dfrac{AC}{AD} = \dfrac{AB}{AC}\).

So \(\dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{AB}{8}\), which gives \(AB = \dfrac{64}{3}\) cm.

\(BD = AB - AD = \dfrac{64}{3} - 3 = \dfrac{55}{3}\) cm.
